prompts.hybrid:
Use case: compositing. Edit the FIRST image, a rough layout assembled from actual Hearts of Iron IV assets. SECOND image is a reference contact sheet of the ACTUAL source sprites; preserve that authentic painted raster-sprite style, NOT the modern 3D/isometric model style. The task is to visually INTEGRATE the original sprite subjects into ONE cohesive clickable industrial works scene, using generated content only to bridge the assets. Keep the recognizable original factory, steam locomotive, construction crane, and documents as the four main subjects; faithfully retain their simplified irregular painted forms, soft low-resolution texture, grey metallic highlights and dark desaturated palette. Keep the original metal UI frame. REMOVE all existing text; the game will draw its own text later. Keep the upper 12% and bottom 10% of the inner panel quiet dark metal for those labels.

Composition: dominant factory in upper-middle/right, locomotive approaching its loading bay from lower-left, short rail track actually meets the bay, crane working immediately to the factory's lower-right. They form one connected compact industrial vignette, not spaced-out icons and not four cards. The relief documents on the left should sit on a small battered timber planning ledge integrated into the same scene, rather than float. Add only the few missing intermediate ground shapes, a loading platform, and a soft shared cast shadow to establish a continuous space. Do not scatter new props. Keep the factory silhouette substantially based on the original supplied factory sprite, not replace it with a new red brick city block. Match the native sprites' schematic painted compression and antique low-resolution game-art texture. No detailed brick joints, realistic roads, sky, skyline, grass, tiny people, realistic architectural render, clean digital line art, black ink outlines or shiny 3D geometry. Grainy hand-painted low-detail sprite collage, grey/charcoal with very restrained tarnished ochre. Broad strong light/shadow patches with softly blended local-color edges, not outlined forms. Original sprites should still be recognizable after integration. The picture must read at just 504x404 pixels. Use coherent scale and lighting, generate the connections around the existing assets, not a wholly unrelated illustration. Aspect ratio 5:4, front-on rectangular steel GUI panel, no text or symbols.
prompts.train_correction:
Precise object correction. FIRST image is the industrial GUI edit target; SECOND image is the existing original HOI4 steam locomotive sprite, a shape/style reference. Edit ONLY the train and the immediately underlying rails in the lower left of image 1. Preserve everything else exactly, including metal frame, factory, documents, crane, smoke, dark palette, composition and soft old painted-game-sprite style.

The current train has malformed wheels/underframe and wheels not sitting correctly on the rails. Replace it with one mechanically coherent short 1930s steam locomotive, based on the simple original reference sprite: cylindrical boiler running lengthwise, a single front circular smokebox facing diagonally toward the lower left, one chimney above the boiler front, driver's cab behind the boiler, solid underframe, three readable large driving wheels on the visible right-hand side connected by ONE simple straight connecting rod. Far-side wheels should be mostly occluded, not another row of wheels pasted across the front. No extra feet-like wheels, duplicated wheel clusters, bent rods or motorcar bumper. The two rails must be parallel in perspective, pass directly beneath the left and right wheels, and continue behind the locomotive through one short coal tender and then the existing box wagons into the factory door. Locomotive, tender and wagons share the same longitudinal axis and receding perspective. Train rear must couple naturally to the wagons. Keep it compact at the original size/location. Keep readable low-detail painted geometry, not photorealism or crisp 3D modelling. No black ink outlines. Do not change any other part of the panel. No text.
